A1.justification: Both complete 29-page PDFs describe HOMER and contain the same main text, references, and Appendices A-H. Text, equations, figures, and tables are readable and directly comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original caption-generation experiments, ablations, and human evaluations in Section 3, with further empirical results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Table 3, human ratings in Table 6, and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The three-role HOMER procedure, retrieval and pruning components, caption generation, Algorithm 1, and Appendix G prompts are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two New Yorker cartoon-caption benchmarks, ImgFlip meme evaluation, and joke-retrieval corpus. No task, dataset, or domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains CoT, Few-shot, Self-consistency, HumorousAI, LoL, Phunny, and CLoT. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the human evaluation and appendix comparisons, including the TF-IDF comparison.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical dataset groups, model configurations, pass@k metrics, evaluator choices, human-evaluation procedures, and matched-call-budget comparisons.

E4.justification: The module, scoring-component, and database-scale ablations are unchanged, as are hyperparameter robustness tests, diversity and toxicity evaluations, leakage analysis, and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-run averaging, human-rating standard deviations, agreement and correlation measures, and Wilcoxon significance tests in Appendix B.13-B.14.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix results. For example, Table 3 retains HOMER's GPT-4o Top10 pass@1/3/5 scores of 66.41/83.70/89.18 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are identical, including Appendix C's theoretical analysis of the relevance-opposition score.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about theory-guided humor generation, creativity, interpretability, and performance. The updated publication-status header does not alter scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including Appendix D's limitation concerning non-humorous images with difficult-to-detect script opposition.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, database curation, evaluator tuning, computational-cost details, and Appendix G prompts are identical. No technical or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 4, Appendix F, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Accepted as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; body wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv margin stamp is repositioned. All figures, tables, captions, and body layouts, including those in the appendices, remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication metadata and the margin stamp but leaves the scientific content and its presentation unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These administrative changes provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
